label: first copy-phase step (input = orig token 0, outputting token 1) in long sequences, mainly L=9
explanation: Fires only at the step right after the first copy output, i.e. the step whose input is original token 0 fed back and whose prev_tok is <DEL> (recall_idx == 1). Never fires in the original or delimiter phases or at any later copy step. Length gates it strongly: 84% of mass at L=9 (t=10, 59% of such steps active), 15% at L=8 (t=9), about 1% at L=7, nothing at L<=6. Magnitude and firing probability depend on the token being fed back (first_tok): f, 0, z, o are highest (top examples are almost all f or 0), then 1, n, b, w. Within L=8 it fires mostly when that token is from this favoured set (adding that clause raises dev F1 from 0.67 to 0.70 and mass recall to 0.96). More digits among the originals slightly raise the rate. The simple predicate covers 84% of mass but has about 41% false positives at L=9, mostly when the fed-back token is a disfavoured letter (m, q, k, e, t, y, i).
